questions.q: What is the key difference between fixed-size and percentage-based FILEGROWTH?
options: Fixed size is a predictable absolute amount every time; percentage compounds based on the file's current size
Fixed size only applies to log files, percentage only to data files
They are functionally identical for files under 1GB
Percentage growth is always faster than fixed-size growth
questions.explain: A fixed FILEGROWTH like 512MB stays the same size regardless of the file's current size, while a percentage grows in absolute terms as the file itself grows larger.

questions.q: Why is percentage growth considered a real anti-pattern on a large file?
options: 10% of a very large file becomes a very large, unpredictable single growth event
Percentage growth is not supported by SQL Server on files over 10GB
It causes the file to shrink instead of grow
It disables Instant File Initialization for that file specifically
questions.explain: Percentage growth compounds: a small percentage of a very large file still becomes a large, slow growth event, which is unpredictable and can block transactions if it's the log.

questions.q: What is the recommended role of autogrowth, per this lesson?
options: A safety net, not the primary sizing strategy — files should be proactively sized for expected growth
The only strategy needed; manual sizing is unnecessary
It should always be disabled entirely
It should only be used for the transaction log, never data files
questions.explain: Files should be sized deliberately upfront, with autogrowth acting as a safety net for unexpected growth rather than the primary way files get their space.

questions.q: Does Instant File Initialization apply to the transaction log file?
options: No — the log file must always be zero-initialized on growth so crash recovery can trust its content
Yes, identically to data files
Only if PAGE_VERIFY is set to CHECKSUM
Only for tempdb's log file, not user databases
questions.explain: IFI applies only to data file growth; the log must always be zero-initialized, which is why an oversized, unpredictable log growth event is a bigger problem than the equivalent for a data file.

questions.q: What Windows privilege does the SQL Server service account need for Instant File Initialization?
options: Perform Volume Maintenance Tasks
Log On as a Service
Act as Part of the Operating System
Bypass Traverse Checking
questions.explain: Instant File Initialization requires the SQL Server service account to hold the 'Perform volume maintenance tasks' Windows right.
